_what: Median days between repeat purchases per RSC consumable, normalised per unit bought. The evidence base for any claim about how long a bundle lasts.
_derived: 2026-07-27, from a paginated pull of ~1,250 paid Shopify orders (all time), grouping line items by customer and product handle.
_these_are_upper_bounds: A reorder gap is consumption time PLUS however long the customer waited, lapsed, or bought elsewhere.
True duration is <= these numbers, never more. So a supply claim at or under the binding rate is defensible;
a claim ABOVE it is not defensible by this data under any reading.
The error is asymmetric in the same direction as the subscription-cadence rule: overstating supply costs the
customer and is the documented reason RSC subscribers churned. When uncertain, claim SHORT.

Where a rate carries `supersedes`, the merchant has given a direct consumption figure and it wins. A reorder gap cannot see consumption; it can only bound it. Prefer product knowledge over a weak gap every time — the deodorant's 90-day gap read as 12 months of supply for a 4-pack and was used to call a subscription plan 3x too aggressive, which was wrong.

TWO of these rates have now been corrected downward by the merchant, and both by a lot: deodorant 90 -> 42, bar soap 47 -> 25. That is not two coincidences, it is the method. A reorder gap measures when somebody got round to buying again, and people put off reordering. Treat every remaining gap-derived rate here (lotion 38, cream 28, toothpaste 61) as a CEILING that is probably well above true consumption, and get a merchant figure before using any of them to set a subscription cadence.
_how_to_use: A bundle lasts as long as the FIRST thing in it runs out — the minimum over its components of (per-unit days x quantity), not the average and not the longest. lib/supply-duration.js does this; do not re-derive it by hand.
_rederive: orders(first:250, query:"financial_status:paid") WITH pagination. lib/shopify.js getOrders() truncates at 250 silently and must not be used for this.

supersedes.why: That 47 was a median REORDER GAP over 14 intervals, not consumption. Sean, 2026-08-02: 'A bar of soap is lasting between 20 and 30 days in the shower.' 25 is the midpoint; the range is kept because a bar's life genuinely varies with how many people use it.

That 90 was a median REORDER GAP over 8 intervals, not consumption. Sean, 2026-08-02: 'There is no way a 2oz deodorant roll on lasts 3 months, six weeks max.' A 42-day use period followed by ~7 weeks of not getting round to reordering produces a 90-day gap exactly, so the measurement and the correction do not conflict — the measurement was always an upper bound and this is the actual figure.

_no_data.coconut-oil-lip-balm: No repeat-purchase intervals. Sold as a four-pack, which further confuses per-unit rate.
